articles.summary: Introducing Critical Materials & Mining Monthly, Sprott’s new report on the market forces shaping critical materials. While October’s weakness underscored miners’ sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions, it did not materially change the sector’s long-term investment thesis. Uranium and copper continued to lead the charge, while supply constraints and structural demand trends continued to provide support for the group.
articles.title: Critical Materials & Mining Monthly: October 2026

articles.summary: Physical gold and gold mining equities can both provide exposure to gold, but they serve different roles in a portfolio. Explore how physical gold may offer diversification and defensive characteristics, while gold miners can provide growth potential and leveraged exposure to rising gold prices, along with additional operational and market risks.
articles.title: Physical Gold or Gold Miners? Two Distinct Ways to Invest in Gold

articles.summary: Gold, silver, uranium and copper are gaining attention as shifting supply-demand dynamics and rising electricity needs reshape the investment landscape. In this interview at Schwab IMPACT 2026, Tom Quigley, Director and Senior Investment Consultant, discusses the forces driving these key metals and how investors can approach physical metals and mining equities.
articles.title: Opportunities in Precious Metals and Critical Materials in Today's Market

articles.summary: Gold’s October pullback appeared to reflect a positioning and liquidity reset more than a weakening of gold demand. Chinese physical buying, gold ETF holdings and official sector demand remained resilient. Silver also faced macro headwinds but continues to benefit from its dual role as a monetary and industrial metal.
articles.title: Gold and Silver Weather a Perfect Storm as Demand Holds Firm

articles.summary: Rare earths are becoming central to defense, electrification, AI and the global race to secure critical supply chains. As China’s export controls expose Western dependence, widening ex-China price premiums and policy support are reshaping the opportunity for alternative producers. We discuss why REXC’s recent decline may reflect a liquidity-driven reset, not weakening rare earth fundamentals.
articles.title: Rare Earths: Strategic Scarcity Meets a Liquidity-Driven Reset
